mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below 97 for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and signals economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE above 6% and a fall in PAYEMS below 135,000,000 in the same month signals labor market overheating with employment saturation, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% AND PAYEMS < 135000000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST of more than 1% signals deteriorating housing and overall demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in FEDFUNDS by more than 0.75 percentage points in a single month signals an aggressive tightening stance, which sharply raises borrowing costs and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO and RSAFS both decline for two consecutive months, it signals a coordinated slowdown in industrial output and retail sales, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, especially in late-cycle regimes.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND RSAFS < previous month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes during late-cycle regimes.
